subject: Mac Pro 1,1 / A1186 storage: boot SSD + 3x 1TB HDD RAID 5 via PCIe for BTC cold storage

facts.claim: Target Mac is a Mac Pro 1,1 / A1186 (2006), Snow Leopard 10.6.8, hostname RevolYOUtionarys-Mac-Pro, user admin. Lion 10.7 install in progress.

source.ref: docs/lion-workflow.json
source.quote: Mac Pro 1,1 / A1186, Snow Leopard 10.6.8, Arctic Fox 47.3 mac32, user admin / hostname RevolYOUtionarys-Mac-Pro

facts.claim: Four independent 3 Gb/s Serial ATA cable-free, direct-attach hard drive bays; four internal hard drive carriers (sleds) included.

source.ref: Apple Mac Pro (Mid 2006) tech specs, support.apple.com/kb/SP30
source.quote: Four independent 3Gb/s Serial ATA cable-free, direct-attach hard drive bays; four internal hard drive carriers included

facts.claim: Bays are numbered 1 through 4 and are stacked top to bottom, bay 1 at the top.

source.ref: Apple SP30 bay listing + Apple service convention
source.quote: Hard drive bay 1 / Hard drive bay 2 / Hard drive bay 3 / Hard drive bay 4

facts.claim: Six SATA ports total: four wired to the drive bays, two unconnected spares (usable with aftermarket extender cables; unsupported under Boot Camp).

source.ref: Apple Fandom Mac Pro 1st generation; Apple Discussions thread 7404111
source.quote: It has a total of six SATA ports – four are connected to the system's drive bays, and two are not connected.

facts.claim: Two 5.25in optical bays. On Mac Pro 1,1 through 3,1 the optical-bay cabling is PATA/ATA-100 (4-pin Molex power), not SATA.

source.ref: Apple Discussions 7404111
source.quote: The cabling in the Optical bays in Mac Pro 1,1 through 3,1 2008 model have ATA/IDE cabling in the Optical bays, with 4-pin molex power connectors

facts.claim: Drives mount on individual trays (sleds) held by captive thumbscrews; no data cable is needed when a drive uses the logic-board bay port.
facts.value: 4 sleds, captive thumbscrews, tool-free bay insert

source.ref: Apple Fandom Mac Pro 1st generation; Apple SP30
source.quote: The hard drives are mounted on individual trays (also known as 'sleds') within the bays by captive thumbscrews

facts.claim: PCI Express expansion: three open full-length slots plus the double-wide 16-lane graphics slot; configurable bandwidth, mechanical support for 16-lane cards, 300 W combined maximum.

source.ref: Apple SP30
source.quote: Three open full-length PCI Express expansion slots ... Configurable bandwidth and mechanical support for 16-lane cards ... 300W combined maximum for all PCI Express slots

facts.claim: Stock lane allocation is 16/4/4/1 and is reconfigurable with the Expansion Slot Utility (options 16/8/1/1, 8/8/8/1, 8/8/4/4).

source.ref: Mac Pro Developer Note quoted on Ars Technica
source.quote: The Mac Pro's standard configuration is one 16-lane, double-wide graphics slot, two 4-lane expansion slots, and one 1-lane expansion slot

facts.claim: Slots run at PCIe Gen1 speed (2.5 GT/s). A RAID card installed in a Mac Pro 1,1 negotiates x4 at 2.5 GT/s.

source.ref: MacRumors: Areca 1880ix-12 on Mac Pro 1,1 (System Profiler dump)
source.quote: Slot: Slot-4 ... Type: RAID Controller, Driver Installed: Yes, Link Width: x4, Link Speed: 2.5 GT/s

facts.claim: Apple software RAID (Disk Utility / diskutil appleRAID) supports only stripe (RAID 0), mirror (RAID 1) and concat (span). RAID 5 is NOT available in Apple software RAID.
facts.value: AppleRAID = stripe | mirror | concat; no RAID 5

source.ref: diskutil man page quoted on Ask Different; AKiTiO RAID guide
source.quote: AppleRAID supports three basic types of RAID sets: stripe (RAID 0), mirror (RAID 1), concat (Spanning)

facts.claim: Of the three AppleRAID types only 'mirror' increases fault tolerance; mirrors can have more than two disks and a spare can be added with diskutil appleRAID add.
facts.value: mirror only fault-tolerant type; spares supported

source.ref: diskutil man page quoted on Ask Different
source.quote: Of these three basic types, only the 'mirror' type increases fault-tolerance.

facts.claim: 3 x 1 TB in RAID 5 yields 2 TB usable ((n-1) x member size) and tolerates the loss of exactly one member.

source.ref: derived: RAID 5 capacity = (n-1) x min member capacity

facts.claim: Areca ARC-1212: PCIe x8 host interface, 4 SAS/SATA ports via one SFF-8087, RAID 0/1/10/3/5/6/JBOD, Intel IOP348 800 MHz, 256 MB DDR2-533 cache.

source.ref: Areca datasheet page / Newegg spec
source.quote: Host Bus Type PCIe x8 ... RAID Level 0, 1, 10, 3, 5, 6, Single Disk or JBOD

facts.claim: Third-party RAID cards do work in a Mac Pro 1,1 under 10.6.8: an Areca ARC-1880ix-12 reported 'Driver Installed: Yes' in Slot-4 at x4 / 2.5 GT/s.

source.ref: MacRumors thread 1218041 (System Profiler dump)
source.quote: Mac OS Version: 10.6.8 ... RAID Controller, Driver Installed: Yes

facts.claim: Apple's optional Mac Pro RAID Card (256 MB cache, 72-hour cache battery) uses RAID Utility rather than Disk Utility and exposes more set types.

source.ref: Apple SP30; Apple Disk Utility documentation quoted by OWC
source.quote: If you have a Mac Pro with a Mac Pro RAID card, use RAID Utility.

facts.claim: Attaching the four internal bay drives to a PCIe SAS/SATA RAID controller requires a breakout/link cable (MaxConnect SAS/SATA Link for 2006/2007 Mac Pro), which is what makes RAID 5/6 in the factory bays possible.

source.ref: MaxUpgrades MaxConnect product page
source.quote: enable user to connect PCI Express SAS/SATA Controllers to the four internal drive bays of the Mac Pro System ... redundancy of RAID 5 or RAID 6

facts.claim: The Bitcoin full chain is past 700 GB as of mid-2026 and keeps growing; pruned nodes validate fully while storing only a few GB.

source.ref: ma.ttias.be full-node post, updated June 2026
source.quote: the full chain is now past 700GB and keeps growing

facts.claim: Cold storage means the spending keys / seed are held offline. A spinning RAID set inside a daily-driver Mac is redundancy, not cold storage, and not a backup.

source.ref: definition; AppleRAID man page agrees
source.quote: AppleRAID is not a replacement for backing up your data.

facts.claim: RAID 5 rebuild must read the whole surviving capacity. On 1 TB consumer drives rated 1e14 bits per unrecoverable read error, a 2 TB rebuild read is roughly a 15% chance of hitting one; enterprise 1e15-rated drives drop that to about 1.5%.

source.ref: derived: P = 1 - exp(-bits_read / URE_rate); manufacturer URE ratings are assumptions, not measurements
